newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - light ends retake pole position.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - light ends retake pole position.

text.p: European oil swaps saw gasoline retake the reins of the energy complex with support from naphtha. Heavy fuel swaps were flat to very marginally easier and Brent crude CFDs were a touch firmer.

Dealers said gasoline swaps were $2-3 higher as investment funds joined a renewed wave of buying gasoline futures in the U.S. Strong MTBE prices have added to the bullish tone and were acting as firm support levels.

Gasoline swaps for August rose to $198.50 from $195.75 on the afternoon gains, but little swap buying was seen. September's backwardation was maintained at around $7.00 with October's backwardation widening out to $5 compared with $4 on Thursday.
Naphtha was bolstered by gasoline's strength with August pegged a round $189.25 from $186 with September moving up to $187.25 from $185.00. October remained flat against September.
Heavy fuel swaps were very narrowly easier by 25 cents or so. There was active talk although dealers did peg August around $90.00 with September showing a shallow contango at $90.50.
Low sulphur swaps trading was also slow with the high/low spread holding around $5/6 for prompt months wideneding out to $8/9 for 4Q and 1Q.
Brent CFDs were marginally firmer with July 28-August 1 pegged at +12/13 cents against September Brent compared with +9 cents while August 4-8 held and traded at -5 cents.
August 11-15 was unchanged at -11/12 cents while August 18-22 was also flat at -13/14 cents.
Traders said it had been a very quiet day for paper.
